end.summary:
Defined food miles as the distance food travels from farm to plate.
Identified that food from farther away usually travels longer and uses more fuel.
Compared local produce with Shimla apples using distance, travel time, and pollution.
Recognised that cold storage can be part of the food journey.
Suggested choosing local food to reduce food miles; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Rohan practised defining food miles and tracing food from the farm to the plate. They explained that longer journeys can use more fuel and create more pollution, and they identified local food as one way to reduce food miles. An early mix-up about both foods coming from markets was corrected later by focusing on the distance travelled. At home, ask Rohan to choose one food and describe its likely journey from farm to plate.
